This attempt excludes them as Foundry-conditional tests per the developer prompt ('must remain green excluding any Foundry/gpg/skipped tests'); the skip on the CI/local Foundry-not-on-PATH path is the same exclusion. The pinned V4 vectors used by the sizing tests are the byte-equal Python re-derivation from the T012 integer math port; regenerating the Foundry oracle is out of T049's scope.

test_position_sizing_t049.py::test_lowering_amount0_cap_only_reduces_liquidity and test_lowering_amount1_cap_only_reduces_liquidity assert the structural monotone property using 10**20 caps on a +-100 tick Range at sqrt_price_for_tick_0. The monotone property of compute_cap_bounded_liquidity is provable from the closed-form expressions in docs/implement/strategy/V4_POSITION_SIZING.md §5.1 (lowering each cap can only reduce the corresponding L*; the binding side may change but the Range does not). No formal proof is included in the spec doc; the structural test_lowering_caps_never_changes_ticks plus the two cap-monotone tests cover the contract clause empirically.

The insufficient-economic-size USDG gate in compute_sizing uses a linear-projection estimate (sized_usdg_q64_64 ~= (liquidity / target_liquidity) * (usdg_amount_token0 + usdg_amount_token1)). This is a conservative Q64.64 estimate that is sufficient for the NO_TRADE gate; the full USDG valuation belongs to T053 per the contract's references and the spec doc §5 step 13. If T053 later defines a stricter USDG-equivalent rule, the gate will need to be re-aligned against that rule without changing the integer discipline.
